history.content: Hi, my phone has no service at all—no bars, nothing loads, and I can't send picture messages. It's completely dead as far as the network goes.

I'm sorry to hear you're experiencing this issue. To help you further, could you please provide your phone number or account details? This will allow me to check your line status and see if there are any network or account-related problems affecting your service.
My phone number is +1-617-555-0148.

Your phone line is currently suspended, which is why you have no service and cannot send or receive messages or calls.

Would you like me to resume your line so you can regain service? If you know the reason for the suspension or if it was done in error, please let me know.
Yes, please resume my line. I'm not sure why it was suspended.

Your line has been resumed and is now active. You should regain service shortly. If your phone does not reconnect to the network within a few minutes, try restarting your device.

If you continue to experience issues or have questions about why your line was suspended, please let me know—I’m here to help!

history.content: My phone rebooted successfully, but I still have no service—no bars, and nothing is loading. What should I try next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your line is now active but you still have no service, let's try a few troubleshooting steps:

1. Check SIM Card: Make sure your SIM card is properly inserted. If possible, remove it, wait a few seconds, and reinsert it.
2. Airplane Mode: Turn Airplane Mode on for 10 seconds, then turn it off.
3. Network Selection: Go to your phone’s network settings and try selecting your carrier manually.
4. Try Another Device: If you have access to another unlocked phone, try inserting your SIM card into it to see if you get service.

If none of these steps work, there may be an issue with your SIM card or device, or there could be a local network outage. Would you like me to check your device details or see if there are any known outages in your area? If you recently changed your device or SIM card, please let me know as well.
I haven't changed my device or SIM card recently. Could you check my device details or see if there are any outages in my area?

Your device (Pixel 8 Pro) is showing as active and there are no recent changes to your SIM or device activation.

To further assist, could you please confirm your current location (city or ZIP code)? This will help me check for any known network outages in your area.
I'm at home in Boston.

Thank you for confirming your location. While I don’t have direct access to real-time network outage maps, your line and device are both active and there have been no recent changes. Since you’re still experiencing no service after a reboot and SIM check, here are a few more steps you can try:

1. Try your SIM card in another unlocked phone (if available) to rule out a device issue.
2. Check if other people in your household or neighborhood with the same carrier are experiencing similar issues.
3. Make sure your phone’s software is up to date.

If you’ve tried these steps and still have no service, the issue may be with your SIM card, device hardware, or a local network problem that isn’t yet reported. At this point, I recommend contacting your carrier’s technical support or visiting a local store for a SIM replacement or further diagnostics.

Would you like me to escalate this issue to a human agent for more specialized troubleshooting?
Before escalating, is there anything else we can check on my phone to troubleshoot the no service issue?

Absolutely! Here are a few more advanced troubleshooting steps you can try on your Pixel 8 Pro before we escalate:

1. Network Reset:
 - Go to Settings > System > Reset options > Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth. This will reset your network settings (you’ll need to re-enter Wi-Fi passwords).

2. Check for Carrier Settings Update:
 - Go to Settings > About phone > SIM status or Carrier settings. If an update is available, install it.

3. Preferred Network Type:
 - Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile network > Preferred network type. Make sure it’s set to 4G/5G (or “Automatic”).

4. APN Settings:
 - Go to Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile network > Access Point Names (APN). Ensure the APN matches your carrier’s recommended settings. If not, you may need to reset or update them.

5. SIM Status:
 - In Settings > About phone > SIM status, check if your phone recognizes the SIM and shows a network.

6. Safe Mode:
 - Try restarting your phone in Safe Mode (hold the power button, then tap and hold “Power off” until you see the Safe Mode prompt). This disables third-party apps that might interfere with connectivity.

If you try these steps and still have no service, please let me know what you observe (especially in SIM status and APN settings). If the issue persists, I can escalate your case to a human agent for further assistance.
Could you walk me through checking my APN settings? I want to make sure they're correct before escalating.

Absolutely! Here’s how you can check and reset your APN (Access Point Name) settings on your Pixel 8 Pro:

1. Open Settings on your phone.
2. Tap on Network & Internet.
3. Tap on Mobile network.
4. Tap on Access Point Names (APN).

Once you’re in the APN menu:

- You should see a list of APNs. Tap on the one that is currently selected (it should have a dot or checkmark next to it).
- Review the details (such as Name, APN, MMSC, MMS Proxy, etc.) and compare them to your carrier’s official APN settings. If you’re not sure what they should be, let me know your carrier and I can provide the correct values.
- If the APN settings look incorrect or are missing, you can reset them:
 • Tap the three dots (⋮) in the upper right corner.
 • Select Reset to default.

After resetting, your phone should automatically load the correct APN settings for your carrier. Restart your phone after making changes.

Let me know if you need the official APN settings for your carrier, or if you notice anything unusual in your APN list!
I’ve opened the APN settings. Would you like me to check the current values, or should I go ahead and reset them to default?

If you haven’t made any manual changes to your APN settings before, it’s usually safe and effective to reset them to default. This will automatically load the correct settings for most carriers and often resolves connectivity issues.

Here’s what I recommend:

- If you see multiple APNs or any unusual/blank entries, go ahead and tap the three dots (⋮) in the upper right corner and select Reset to default.
- After resetting, restart your phone to apply the changes.

If you prefer, you can also check and share the current APN values with me before resetting, and I can verify if they match your carrier’s recommended settings.

Would you like to reset now, or would you like to share your current APN details for review?

I’ve already reset the APN settings to default and rebooted my phone. The message said the settings were reset (APN: internet, MMSC URL: http://mms.carrier.com/mms) and that the device rebooted successfully. I still have no service—no bars and nothing loads.

You’ve completed all the recommended troubleshooting steps, and your line and device are active, but you still have no service. I am now transferring you to a human agent for advanced support and a deeper investigation into your issue. Thank you for your patience—help is on the way!
